chapter: California, Art Tatum and Lionel Hampton
title: Arriving in California and revering Art Tatum
summary: He did no studio work, kept studying, and in California met Art Tatum, whom he calls the lord and god of music.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: Yes. Well, look then when you got to the coast with Lloyd Hunter -- no you got to the coast with Floyd Ray rather, and you did studio sessions. Did you stay with Floyd Ray's band, do you remember that.
You came to California and you moved into studio work?

No, no, that's not true. I didn't play studio work. There again as I said, I was still learning, I was still -- I considered myself to be actually still in my embryo stage of learning. I was slowly learning. I had learned how to write music, but I still was not sure that I was a competent writer. I knew I was writing to write notes, but I didn't have the real professional feeling where I would say I was in demand by the famous orchestras. I hadn't learned that yet.

I was still learning, still studying. I kept my head in the books, I kept my head in the library of music, I kept listening to music. And not only that, but this is where at the time when I got to California that I met Art Tatum.
The lord and god of not only the piano but music.
That's right. To me Art Tatum says everything there is to be said about jazz music.
If there is such a man that ever lived
that could be an example of the true expression and beauty of music, it was Art Tatum. You know?
And I say that with all humility and humble respect that you would have for the Lord himself.
Yes. How did you meet him? You heard him play.
